meta.title: Improve small metadata allocations
meta.body_summary: Introduce SingleItemReadOnlyDictionary optimized for single key/value pairs and use it in Error constructors and Result helpers to reduce small metadata allocations.

perf_labels.notes: Codex introduced SingleItemReadOnlyDictionary to reduce allocations; merged rapidly by author with no review or benchmark evidence.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 356 changed lines across 10 files, this is a small-to-medium edit by absolute volume. It fits an incremental optimization PR that was merged quickly by the author without review.

review_details.performance_claim: Reduce allocations for small metadata by using a specialized SingleItemReadOnlyDictionary.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: The PR requires domain-specific C# knowledge to create a low-allocation replacement for Dictionary when only one key-value pair is expected; Codex successfully implemented and integrated it across multiple files.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No benchmark, profiling, or allocation metrics provided; only a test command for correctness, not performance validation.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: No regression handling; PR merged directly.

core_change_summary.description: Introduced SingleItemReadOnlyDictionary<TKey, TValue> in src/LightResults/Common/SingleItemReadOnlyDictionary.cs, then used it in Error constructors (Error.cs) and Result helpers (Result.cs, Result`1.cs) to replace full Dictionary instantiation with a lightweight single-entry container.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Merge from feature/work also brought in README updates, interface tweaks, and test adjustments; these are likely pre-existing changes and not part of the perf optimization.
change_trajectory: Initial commit adds SingleItemReadOnlyDictionary and replaces Dictionary usage in Error, Result, Result<TValue>.
Merge commit from feature/work introduces additional interface and test changes; merged within 14 minutes total.

collaboration_trajectory: Author jscarle merged immediately without any review or comment.
